correctness.rationale: PASS: Under 0<f<p<1 the exact finite-history mixture likelihood has I_k=(1-R_k)/[psi(1-psi)], with 0<I_k<=1/[psi(1-psi)]. Above the KL threshold a law of large numbers makes R_k vanish. Uniformly below (1-epsilon) log(1/psi)/d, the explicit positive fractional moment of P_k/Q_k bounds 1-R_k by exp(-c log(1/psi)); at all k above (1+epsilon) log(1/psi)/d the complete-data information bound forces loss versus a near-threshold construction. The comparison proves all maximizing k have the unique normalized asymptotic and establishes the sharp maximal-information coefficient. For f=0, any-detection is Bernoulli(psi a_k), yielding I_k=a_k/[psi(1-psi a_k)] and, by strict concavity, unique k=1 at the displayed explicit threshold. A clean stdlib script independently tested 72 exact rational identity cases and 84 f=0 cases, plus four finite diagnostics. It does not substitute computation for the infinite proof.

None gives or implies the calibrated-positive-false-positive rare-occupancy optimal-revisit KL coefficient and information limit with the singular exactly-zero-false-positive contrast; models with nuisance detection estimated have different Fisher objectives. Publicly accessible related mathematical research reports concern N-mixture identifiability, species discovery, or distinct Bernoulli divergence questions, and do not establish the stated constrained optimum. General optimal binary-mixture block-design theory may still cover this result and priority is not independently certified.

value.rationale: PASS: Rare species with imperfect species-identification face a genuine field-design question: how to divide a unit-cost visit budget between repeated checks on a site and sampling additional sites. The result gives a sharp parameter-sensitive, non-trivial optimal scaling with the Bernoulli relative-entropy constant and exhibits a discontinuous qualitative design change at zero false-positive probability. It distinguishes two biological error mechanisms and clarifies when the conventional survey-more-sites advice does not extrapolate to rare species. It is a theorem for homogeneous known-detection Fisher-optimal design only, not an empirical general conservation recommendation.
